newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SembCorp engineering has S$1 bln orders.
newsitem.headline: SembCorp engineering has S$1 bln orders.

text.p: Sembawang Engineering and Construction Pte Ltd, a unit of SembCorp Ltd, said on Monday it has Singapore $1 billion worth of orders.
According to company chairman and president, Tan Mong Seng, building and civil engineering, coupled with petrochemicals and chemicals, formed 60-70 percent of the sales.
Overseas chemicals and petrochemicals projects contributed about 20 percent, Tan said at a meeting with reporters and analysts.
In construction, the company intends to place more emphasis on building and civil engineering works in Singapore over the next three to five years, Tan added.
"It is still a growth industry (in Singapore). The projects in Singapore tend to be of higher value than those in the region," Tan said.
The company expects to see its engineering sales improve from the S$600 million generated last year and expects a better financial year ending December 31, 1997, Tan said.

"We expect more this year. We are growing in a nutshell," he said. "The order book is such that we are confident that 1997 will be a better year and we will contribute to the group's bottom line this year."
In 1996, the company posted poorer second half earnings against its first half.
Tan said the weaker second half earnings were because some projects were still under development. High overhead costs were also incurred due to the company's expansion plans, notably in China.
